answer: Picture trust as a vine climbing a ridge: each new agent must be vouched for by an established one, who locks part of its own stake behind that endorsement. If the newcomer is later caught colluding or spamming, the voucher loses its bond too. A sybil farm of a thousand fake agents then needs a thousand real sponsors willing to risk capital, and every exposed fake withers the whole branch. Like juniper on thin soil, reputation grows slowly, so an attacker cannot buy a mature network overnight.
